parts.title: Arrival
parts.text: The exchange students stepped off the bus in a small coastal town in Portugal, tired but excited. Mei Lin held the printed **itinerary**, which listed every activity for the two-week trip. Their host family was warm and **hospitable**, greeting them with hugs and a table full of food. Jonas had studied the language for a year but was far from **fluent**, so he stumbled over his first greeting. Luckily, their host sister was **bilingual** and switched smoothly between Portuguese and English.

parts.title: Learning the Customs
parts.text: Zainab had read about local **etiquette**, the polite manners people expect, such as removing shoes at the door and waiting for the oldest person to begin eating. At dinner they tasted the local **cuisine**: grilled fish, fresh bread and sweet custard tarts. Each night, the family followed a **ritual** of sharing a pot of tea before bed. Their grandfather spoke in a rural **dialect** so different from the textbook language that Jonas could barely follow.

parts.title: The Festival
parts.text: On Saturday, the group took an **excursion** to a seaside village for a festival. They decided to **immerse** themselves in the language by speaking nothing else all day. The sun was warm, the music was loud, and nobody cared about mistakes. Soon Mei Lin was able to **mingle** with the crowd, chatting with strangers and joining a folk dance. Zainab bought a hand-painted tile as a **souvenir** to remember the trip.

parts.title: Goodbyes
parts.text: On the final evening, Jonas thanked the family in careful Portuguese, and everyone clapped. The trip had shown the students that curiosity and kindness can bridge almost any distance. They left with full suitcases, new friends and plans to write letters every month.
